newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT- Sept T-bond consolidation seen continuing.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT- Sept T-bond consolidation seen continuing.

text.p: U.S. September Treasury bond continued its consolidative mood Thursday, still working off overbought conditions, traders said.

September rallied to a fresh four-month high at 112-13/32 in a delayed reaction to a rise in the latest weekly jobless claims, but cut its gains after a strong Philadelphia Federal Reserve business index.
Some traders said the market was tired out from recent gains and needed to consolidate.
They said the market for the time being was confined between 112-16/32 resistance and 111-16/32 support.

"For the session we have a little bit of a negative bias going forward," said David Ging, technical analyst with DLJ Securities. He noted that September got close to resistance at 112-16/32 but failed to get through it, "keeping it under a little bit of pressure today."
But support at 111-17/32 to 18/32 was expected to hold, Ging said.
"We're under some short-term pressure but it's a buying opportunity," Ging said. "111-17/32 to 18/32 is expected to hold and we should get a rally from there close to 113-00."
February 18's 113-9/32 high is the peak for the year.
Several analysts agreed that an intermediate-term uptrend remained intact, and said any pressure late this week sets the market up for gains again next week.

"It's still an uptrend," said Jim Hyercyzk, president of JAH Research and Trading. He noted that a lower close in September T-bond futures Thursday would constitute a daily reversal, a mildy bearish technical pattern.
"This won't be a change in trend but it will indicate a reversal which means three to five days down," Hyercyzk said.
The analysts also said they were watching for any signs a correction lower could be sharper than first thought.
Hyercyzk said a break through 111-17/32 would set September up for a correction at least to 110-15/32.
DLJ's Ging said given the overly high level of bullish sentiment, "if you do see it start to deteriorate you could be in for a substantial correction."

And David Hightower, president of the Hightower Report, said declining open interest during September's recent gains was a clue that "the herd is not voting in favor of this rally continuing forever."
